method: Review only the 31 previously pending phrases using existing source paragraphs. Preserve completed entries and historical Unit 1 coverage decisions; source allegations, metaphor and personification remain distinct from teaching examples.
phrases: am I allowed to
asking whether a rule or person permits an action
我可以……吗；允许我……吗
Am I allowed to use this entrance?
我可以走这个入口吗？
Allowed to + base verb concerns permission, not physical ability. Source question does not establish whether the student had a legal right to stand there.
follow-up questions
additional questions that clarify or explore an earlier answer
追问；后续问题
We asked follow-up questions about the proposed schedule.
我们就提议的日程追问了几个问题。
Follow-up is hyphenated before questions; follow up as a verb has no hyphen. Source requests further scrutiny rather than endorsing the conclusion.
get hit by a car
be struck by a car
被汽车撞到
The safety lesson discusses how pedestrians can get hit by a car.
安全课讨论行人可能遭汽车撞击的情况。
Get-passive emphasizes the event; by identifies the cause. The phrase describes contact, not who is legally at fault.
get the answer
receive or discover the response to a question
得到答案；弄清答案
We should get the answer by tomorrow.
我们应该明天就能得到答案。
Get can mean learn or receive. Source uses irony about an outcome answering a question; do not replace it with a new factual claim.
go zero to 60
accelerate from a standstill to sixty miles per hour in the conventional U.S. car expression
从静止加速到每小时六十英里
The review measures how quickly the car can go from zero to sixty.
评测测量了汽车从静止加速到每小时六十英里需要多久。
Source omits from in casual speech and explicitly says the car is not performing this test. Do not infer the actual collision speed from the idiom.
have to be
must be, sometimes expressing a strong inference rather than obligation
一定是；必定处于……状态
There has to be a reason for the delay.
延误一定有原因。
Source's you have to be expresses emphatic inference about bad luck, not a literal requirement to become unlucky.
in front of
in a position ahead of or before the front surface of something
在……前面
Please wait in front of the building.
请在楼前等候。
Spatial relation depends on the reference object. Do not confuse in front of a car with behind it elsewhere in the narrated sequence.
kind of
somewhat, approximately or in a softened way, informally
有点；算是；大概（口语）
The instructions are kind of confusing.
这些说明有点让人困惑。
Hedge or degree softener here, not a kind of meaning a type of. Its presence does not remove the profanity or evaluative stance of the original sentence.
little more like
slightly closer to a particular comparison
更有点像……
The sound was a little more like a knock than a click.
那个声音更有点像敲击声，而不是咔嗒声。
Usually a little more like + comparison. Source's bonk is a casual impact description; comparison is not a measured force or medical assessment.
parking lot
an area where vehicles can be parked
停车场
The meeting point is next to the parking lot.
集合点在停车场旁边。
Common American term; distinguishes the whole area from a single parking spot.
some sort of
an unspecified or approximate kind of something
某种；某一类
There seems to be some sort of misunderstanding.
似乎存在某种误会。
Hedges classification. Source's luck recession is a creative metaphor, not an established economic condition affecting a person.
sooner rather than later
relatively soon, preferably without delay
尽早；早点而不是拖到以后
We should discuss the issue sooner rather than later.
我们应该尽早讨论这个问题。
No precise deadline. Source uses an ironic retrospective description of how quickly events answer a question.
back into
move backward into or against something
倒着驶入；倒退着碰到
She carefully backed into the parking space.
她小心地倒车进入停车位。
Source back into him concerns backward movement toward contact, not entering an empty space. The surrounding reversing back is conversational redundancy.
fall over
lose an upright position and fall to the ground
摔倒；倒下
The empty chair fell over in the wind.
空椅子被风吹倒了。
Source negates the action; not falling over does not prove absence of injury or settle fault.
get dragged
be pulled along a surface or through a situation
被拖着走；被拖拽
The suitcase got dragged through the mud.
行李箱被拖过了泥地。
Physical dragging in source, not dragged into an argument. Source explicitly says this did not happen.
get out of
leave or move out of a place
离开；从……出来
We need to get out of the room before it is locked.
房间上锁前，我们需要出去。
Physical exit here; elsewhere get out of doing something can mean avoid a duty. Source concerns the car leaving its space.
lose balance
become unable to stay steady or upright
失去平衡
She almost lost her balance on the uneven path.
她在不平的路面上差点失去平衡。
Lose one's balance is the more usual full collocation; source omits the possessive. Negated balance loss does not establish injury severity.
no longer come back
not return anymore, with a preceding modal or context determining why
不再回来；不再能返回
After the move, he could no longer come back every weekend.
搬家后，他无法再每个周末都回来了。
Source can no longer come back describes a reported restriction, not a voluntary choice. Keep the modal when interpreting the fragment.
reversing out of
driving backward out of a space
倒车驶出
The driver was reversing out of the garage.
司机正在倒车驶出车库。
Movement direction, not changing a decision. Source's anticlimactically is the narrator's evaluation, not a speed measurement.
run over
pass over a person or object with a vehicle's wheels
用车轮碾过
The empty box was run over by a delivery cart.
空箱子被送货推车碾过了。
Vehicle-wheel sense, not run over a document quickly. Source says allegedly about the foot; no injury finding is independently supplied.
the entire year
the whole year-long period being discussed
整整一年；整个年度
The pass is valid for the entire year.
这张通行证全年有效。
Entire emphasizes the whole period. Source's potentially ran over is nonstandard participle wording retained in the quote, not reproduced as teaching grammar.
not super aggressive
not extremely forceful or confrontational, informally
并不是特别强硬或激烈
The reminder was firm but not super aggressive.
提醒的语气很坚定，但并不是特别强硬。
Super is an informal degree intensifier; not super aggressive does not mean entirely gentle or harmless.
start moving
begin to move or cause something to move
开始移动；开始开动
Wait for the signal before you start moving the equipment.
等收到信号后再开始移动设备。
Start + -ing; source is a cautionary hypothetical about moving a vehicle, not an instruction to drive toward people.
the ones to blame
the people considered responsible for something bad
该负责任的人；被认为有过错的人
The review asked who the ones to blame really were.
评估追问真正该负责的人是谁。
Blame is responsibility attribution, not automatically legal guilt. Source's it was decided is a reported decision whose basis the narrator questions.
there's a bunch of
there is a group or a fairly large number, informally
有一群；有不少
There's a bunch of people waiting outside.
外面有一群人在等候。
Common spoken singular agreement with a bunch; neutral alternative there are many people. No exact count is implied.
this isn't just
this is more significant or specific than the ordinary description that follows
这不只是……；这并非普通的……
This isn't just a schedule change; it affects the whole team.
这不只是日程调整，它影响整个团队。
Just restricts significance. Source adds any parking lot to stress the institutional context, not to deny that it is a parking lot.
try to do something
attempt to take some action
设法采取行动；尝试做点什么
We should try to do something about the noise.
我们应该设法处理一下噪声问题。
Try to + verb attempts an action; try -ing can test a method. Source leaves the alternative action broad rather than specifying an authorized procedure.
standing in the way
standing where someone or something needs to pass
站在路上挡住通行
A box was standing in the way of the doorway.
一个箱子挡在门口。
Physical obstruction here; figurative stand in the way of progress means hinder it. Source's standing people are not assigned intent by the phrase alone.
get out of the parking spot
move a vehicle out of its individual parking space
把车驶出停车位
The driver waited for a clear path to get out of the parking spot.
司机等通道畅通后才把车驶出停车位。
Spot is one space, not the entire parking lot. Source's personification of the car is preserved without inferring autonomous-driving technology.
at fault
responsible for an error, problem or harmful event
有过错；应负责任
The review will examine whether the process was at fault.
评估将检查是否是流程出了问题。
Be at fault is a responsibility judgment; source questions how one was assigned and does not independently establish liability.
no longer
not anymore after a previous state or possibility
不再
The old link no longer works.
旧链接已经不能用了。
Placed before a main verb or after be; source combines it with can to describe a changed permission or ability, not merely present location.
